source.title: Exact expressions for double descent and implicit regularization via surrogate random design
source.authors: Michal Derezinski; Feynman T. Liang; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: Analyzes double descent with exact non-asymptotic expressions for a minimum-norm linear estimator and empirical comparisons, rather than the neural-network width-sweep method in V2.
record.gate_note: The paper studies linear regression as feature dimension and sample size vary. It does not test the claim's specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks or datasets.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes minimum-norm linear regression, not neural-network widening or any other behavior specified by V1–V8. Its double-descent results concern parameter-estimation MSE, E||ŵ−w*||², rather than held-out classification error. These related results do not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors derive exact non-asymptotic parameter-estimation MSE expressions for their surrogate design, reproduce linear-regression double descent, establish asymptotic agreement with specified i.i.d. designs, and show that the surrogate minimum-norm estimator equals a population ridge solution in expectation in the underdetermined regime.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes minimum-norm linear regression using a determinantal surrogate design, with empirical comparisons to standard i.i.d. designs; it does not use the neural-network training recipes in V2.
record.method_sensitivity: The MSE curve's underdetermined-regime shape changes with the feature covariance spectral decay; empirical discrepancies are examined across four eigenvalue decay profiles.

fits_no_version.finding: The surrogate-design linear estimator exhibits double descent as expected sample size crosses d; empirical i.i.d. Gaussian estimates broadly follow the surrogate curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimum-norm linear regression can exhibit double descent in parameter-estimation MSE, with curve shape depending on feature covariance.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 also varies feature dimension d with n fixed at 100. Thus the record's suggestion that the study lacks a fixed-sample dimension sweep is incorrect, although this remains a linear-regression experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed sample size, minimum-norm linear regression's parameter-estimation MSE depends nonmonotonically on feature dimension and covariance spectrum.

fits_no_version.finding: Empirical bias and variance discrepancies decrease approximately as O(1/d) at fixed aspect ratios; the general rate is conjectured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Surrogate-design MSE expressions approximate i.i.d. Gaussian linear-regression MSE increasingly accurately as dimension grows.

record.problems: Exact MSE expressions are derived for the non-i.i.d. surrogate design. Comparisons with i.i.d. designs are empirical or asymptotic; the study does not evaluate neural networks or natural-label classification accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were left out.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy in the same architectures and training recipes.
Neural-network widening beyond zero training error and its effect on held-out error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The different model and measure establish noncoverage, not a limits_scope verdict on V2. Double descent is observed in the study's own setting; cannot_determine denotes the rows' inability to establish any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization in the specified architectures and datasets.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10, and widening networks at fixed training-set size.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Moore-Penrose estimator
rows.operation_detail: Varied sample size n across underdetermined, interpolation, and overdetermined regimes; exact MSE derived for surrogate random design.

conditions.value: isotropic and non-isotropic Gaussian feature covariance; condition numbers κ=1, 1e2, 1e5

rows.value: The paper reports an MSE peak at n=d and states that moving away from the threshold in either direction tends to reduce generalization error.
rows.note: The exact expression is for the surrogate design; Figure 1 compares it with empirical estimates under the i.i.d. Gaussian design.
rows.check: The double-descent result is for a linear estimator and parameter-estimation MSE, so it cannot establish V2. Under the surrogate design, n is expected sample size; realized sample size is random except at n=d. Figure 1's null-estimator baseline is MSE=1.

rows.subject: Moore-Penrose estimator under standard i.i.d. design
rows.operation_detail: Empirically varied sample size n and compared observed MSE with surrogate-design expressions.

conditions.value: isotropic and non-isotropic Gaussian feature covariance; condition numbers κ=1, 1e2, 1e5

rows.value: Empirical estimates closely match the surrogate expressions; the plotted curves show the double-descent peak at n=d.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars are three times the standard error of the mean.
rows.note: No precise curve values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The empirical curves concern linear regression and parameter-estimation MSE, not neural-network width and held-out error. The agreement with surrogate expressions is a valid methodological result but bears on no listed version. Figure 1 includes the null-estimator baseline MSE=1.

rows.subject: Moore-Penrose estimator under standard i.i.d. design
rows.operation_detail: Increased feature dimension while keeping n/d fixed and measured discrepancy between i.i.d.-design MSE and surrogate expressions.

conditions.value: four eigenvalue decay profiles: exponential, linear, fixed-degree polynomial, variable-degree polynomial

rows.measure: Variance and bias discrepancies from surrogate MSE expressions
rows.value: In all cases, the discrepancies decay to zero at rate O(1/d).
rows.note: This supports asymptotic consistency of the surrogate expressions with i.i.d.-design MSE, not a neural-network width sweep.
rows.check: Discrepancies between surrogate formulas and i.i.d.-design bias and variance measure approximation accuracy, not whether widening improves generalization. The stated d=10–1000 range applies to the variance experiment; the bias experiment uses a smaller range. The numbers_found value '1/1' is erroneous; the reported empirical decay is O(1/d).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Linear minimum-norm regression in the reported Gaussian and sub-Gaussian design settings
reader_labels.reason: The study reports a double-descent peak at the interpolation threshold, but its model and sweep differ from V2's specified ReLU width experiments (R1–R3).
